guidelines.detail: refines GW-06 (The description makes site visits conditional while naming other investigation activities, and the reported parallel-join deadlock shows synchronization waited for an inactive branch. This applies the documented inclusive-join guideline specifically to a mix of required and conditional activities.)

refines FID-01 (The description specifies a distinct activity triggered by a condition, but the reference task has no counterpart in the generated model. FID-01 already requires modeling every described activity; this guideline refines it by specifying where to place a condition-triggered activity.)

same as LRN-012 (The label pairs and description support preserving which participant performs the stated action and its direction. This is consistent with the learned guideline to preserve the described action in the BPMN label rather than substitute a related action.)

documentation rule GW-06 not applied (The description distinguishes required investigation activities from site visits that occur only in certain cases. The validator reports a deadlock at a parallel join waiting for flows that cannot receive a token. GW-06 already says to use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.)

same as LRN-005 (The missing flows show breaks in stated transitions from an activity to review logic, from resubmission back into review, and from approval to the subsequent activity. LRN-005 already gives essentially the same sequence-preservation guidance.)
same as LRN-018 (The description says the regional office submits documents, while the generated label describes receiving them. LRN-018 already gives the same sender-perspective guidance.)

same as LRN-031 (The deadlock shows a parallel join waiting for branches that the description says may not occur: site visits are performed only in certain cases, while the later report follows completion of the work. This matches learned guideline LRN-031. Documented guideline GW-06 also supports synchronizing only activated reachable branches.)

same as LRN-001 (The description identifies approval and return for revision as alternatives, while the reference includes a distinct approval activity and its connecting flows that are absent from the generated model. This is already covered in substance by LRN-001, which requires modeling an approval on the stated branch before a later activity.)

same as LRN-012 (The description states specific actions and outcomes, while the label pairs show wording that may shift or blur those distinctions. The proposed guidance is already essentially captured by learned guideline LRN-012.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names multiple activities that must all occur and another activity that occurs only in certain cases as part of the same stage: Model the required activities and the conditional activity so synchronization waits for all required work but only for conditional branches that were activated; use an inclusive split and join rather than a parallel join that waits for every possible branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names multiple activities that must all occur and another activity that occurs only in certain cases as part of the same stage

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a condition triggers a distinct activity: Model the activity as a task on the branch where the condition holds; do not omit it or represent it only as a branch outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a condition triggers a distinct activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or end event with a concise phrase that preserves the stated action or outcome; do not substitute a related action or add an unsupported one.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description attributes an activity to a participant and distinguishes that participant’s action or transfer direction from a related action by another participant

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that several activities in a stage are all required, while another activity in that stage occurs only in certain cases

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents distinct activities in an ordered progression, including transitions into, through, or out of branches or synchronization points: Connect each consecutive activity with a sequence flow, preserving the stated transitions through branches and synchronization points.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description specifies an ordered progression of activities that includes a decision, review, or repeated step and states what follows

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one participant sends information to another participant: Model and label the activity from the sender’s perspective as sending the information, rather than as the recipient receiving it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one participant sends or submits information to another

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a conditional outcome followed by intervening actions or an approval before a later activity: Model the branch through the described intervening actions and approval in the stated order; do not connect it directly to a later activity that bypasses them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a decision-maker may approve an item or return it for changes before it proceeds to a later step
